name: AD8510 / AD8512 (ADI precision JFET-input dual)
tagline: ADI's 8 MHz JFET-input dual with 8 nV/√Hz noise and 0.0005% THD+N. A Chinese DIY forum post compares its sound to the AD823 and says it suits headphone amps.
technology: Precision JFET-input op-amp: very low noise (8 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz), low input bias current, 8 MHz GBW, 20 V/µs slew, dual supply ±5 V to ±15 V. Comes as single (AD8510), dual (AD8512) and quad (AD8513).

part_numbers.notes: Single. Covered by the shared AD8510/AD8512/AD8513 datasheet. Recalled from memory, not web-confirmed: A and B offset grades in SOIC-8 (R) and MSOP-8 (RM), e.g. AD8510ARZ, AD8510ARMZ, AD8510BRZ.

Dual; this is the catalogue's lead part. ADI lists its status as Production. AD8512ARZ is confirmed (Octopart datasheet link). AD8512ARMZ (MSOP-8) and AD8512BRZ (B grade, tighter Vos) are recalled from memory and unconfirmed. Older non-RoHS parts without the Z suffix (AD8512AR/ARM/BR) are probably obsolete (unconfirmed).
Quad. Added to the datasheet later, because early editions are titled 'AD8510/AD8512' only. Packages are SOIC-14 and TSSOP-14 (from memory, unconfirmed).
Enhanced Product (defense/aerospace flow) version of the dual, with its own separate datasheet (radiolocman listing). Status not checked.

lineage.period: early 2000s to present (introduction year not confirmed)
lineage.notes: The datasheet reached Rev. K in January 2010. The earliest editions covered only the AD8510/AD8512 (RS mirror title); the AD8513 quad was added later.

PCN 25_0156 lists AD8510/AD8512/AD8513 part numbers. It moves production to an existing qualified process at ADI's Camas, WA fab to secure supply. The previous fab is not stated in the search summaries.

reputation.summary: This is a niche, tier-C reputation. The main praise found is a single post in a Chinese erji.net thread ('谈谈自己用过的一些运放', op-amps I have used). The poster says it sounds almost the same as the AD823, with more output current and lower supply current. They call it slightly harsh but 'not unpleasant and equally appealing', and think it works in headphone amps. No wider consensus in Western audio forums was confirmed in this pass.
sonic_descriptors: close to AD823 (per one erji.net poster)
slightly harsh / forward but not unpleasant (same source)
typical_uses: op-amp swaps in DIY headphone amplifiers (erji.net report)
general low-noise JFET-input audio gain stages (inferred from specs)
caveats: Praise comes from a single forum source and should not be generalised.
Needs at least ±5 V (about 10 V total). The output is not rail-to-rail.
Sold only in SMD packages (SOIC/MSOP/TSSOP), so DIP sockets need an adapter.
JFET input bias current roughly doubles for every 10 °C rise, so it is best kept away from hot spots.

silicon_changes.identification: Not established. The search summaries did not show a date-code or trace-code cutover, so check the PCN's effective date and date codes.
silicon_changes.summary: Wafer-fab change: production of the listed AD8510/AD8512/AD8513 part numbers uses an existing qualified process at ADI's Camas, WA fab to ensure continuous supply. ADI says it expects no impact on fit, form, function or reliability. The datasheet was not revised (still Rev. K).
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None claimed by ADI; datasheet limits are unchanged. As with any fab or process move, typical noise, bias-current and offset distributions could shift within those limits, which is not verified.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same part numbers and datasheet limits, and the vendor states no fit/form/function change

counterfeit_notes: No specific counterfeit reports for this family were found in this pass. It is a mid-price SMD-only ADI JFET part, so relabelled or reclaimed units on marketplace listings are a generic risk. Buy from authorised distributors and check the ADI marking and date codes.

claims_confirmed: The current ADI datasheet is AD8510/AD8512/AD8513 Rev. K (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8510_8512_8513.pdf).
Rev. K is listed as dated 01/21/2010 (https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/pdf.html?di=170505).

PCN 25_0156 lists AD8510/AD8512/AD8513 part numbers and describes using an existing qualified process at ADI's Camas, WA fab, with no expected fit/form/function/reliability impact (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/7560/ADI_PCN_25_0156_Rev_-_Form.pdf).
Specs of 8 MHz GBW, 20 V/µs slew, 7.6 nV/√Hz at 10 kHz and 0.0005% THD+N (1 kHz, G=+1, RL=2k), with AD8512 status Production (https://www.analog.com/en/products/ad8512.html).

Front-page specs: 8 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz, 400 µV max Vos, 1 µV/°C TCVos, 25 pA Ib, 500 ns settling to 0.1%, ±5 V to ±15 V (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8510_8512_8513.pdf).
An early edition titled 'AD8510/AD8512' (no AD8513) is mirrored by RS (https://docs.rs-online.com/17b1/0900766b801ce1ae.pdf).

revision_chain_notes: Analog Devices AD8510_8512 / AD8510_8512_8513, known so far (oldest to newest): Rev. 0 (date unknown, no copy found). Rev. A (date unknown, early 2000s; AD8510/AD8512 only). The RS Components mirror docs.rs-online.com/17b1/0900766b801ce1ae.pdf, already listed as 'unknown', holds Rev. A: its search result title shows the 'REV. A' footer. Revs. B through J are missing: no dates, copies or change lists were found. The AD8513 quad was added somewhere in B-J, and the revision that added it is unknown. Rev. K is dated 2010-01-21 (analog.com current, radiolocman di=170505). New mirrors whose revision was not shown: alldatasheet 83235 (AD8510, a sibling of 83236 and probably early), alldatasheet 1957163 (a later upload), radiolocman data.html?di=350333, datasheetbank and datasheetall. A separate document, AD8512-EP, has Rev. 0 (date unknown) on Mouser. Later EP revisions are unknown. Archive seeds: the uppercase analog.com media URL was seen in search summaries. The http://www.analog.com/static/imported-files/data_sheets/AD8510_8512_8513.pdf seed was built from ADI's standard legacy path pattern and was not seen in results, so treat it as unverified. Still missing: Rev. 0 and Revs. B-J (dates, change lists, copies), the revision that first added the AD8513, the Rev. J to K change summary, and any pre-2004 'UploadedFiles' URLs on analog.com. There were no second sources or acquirer re-issues: ADI is the sole source.
